title: Raising the Rate on a Bump-Up Certificate of Deposit
content:
On a tier of the Certificates of Deposit line whose published count of rate increases stands above zero, the owner may ask once in a term for the rate to be raised.

## 1. What must hold

Three things must hold together, and a request is declined with no change to the certificate where any fails:

- the certificate is active;
- the one rate increase the term allows has not already been used;
- the tier's currently published standard annual percentage yield is higher than the certificate's own annual percentage yield less the bonus points already applied in this term.

The third is a comparison of like with like: the published standard yield carries no bonus points, so the certificate's yield is stripped of the points it carries before the two are set against each other.

## 2. The window in which a request is accepted

A request is accepted only within the calendar months the tier publishes after the current term started. Months are counted from the term start date, and the request is accepted while the current date is on or before the term start date plus that number of calendar months, falling back to the last day of the month where that day does not exist. The term start date is read from the certificate record.

### Boundary readings, on hypothetical dates

| Term start date | Window | Last day a request is accepted | On that day | On the day after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 January 2024 | 15 months | 20 April 2025 | accepted | declined |
| 31 January 2024 | 15 months | 30 April 2025 | accepted | declined |

The second row shows the fallback at work: there being no 31 April, the window closes on the last day of that month.

## 3. The rate that results

The new rate and annual percentage yield are the published standard rate and yield plus the same bonus points already in the rate. They take effect from the date of the request, and interest already accrued before that date is not reworked.

*Hypothetical:* a certificate carries 3.98 percent, of which 0.15 points are bonus. The tier now publishes a standard rate of 4.10 percent. The new rate is 4.25 percent, being the published 4.10 plus the same 0.15 points, from the day of the request onward.
